section: Social Studies (Paper-2) · Ch46 — Ancient & Medieval India
subject: Social Studies
stem: The Mughal emperor who introduced 'Din-i-Ilahi' (a syncretic religious philosophy blending elements of various faiths), abolished the pilgrimage tax on non-Muslims, and whose court included the legendary 'Navaratnas' (nine gems) like Birbal and Tansen, was:
explanation: Akbar, known for religious tolerance and administrative reforms, introduced Din-i-Ilahi and maintained a court of celebrated Navaratnas — in contrast to Aurangzeb's later reversal of these tolerant policies.
